findings.reason: a node briefed on "the write changes the document digest" builds a guard against a digest that already excludes declarations, so it either lands a no-op or instruments a comparison no production path makes, and the real trigger (a landing collapse replacing the section's authored prose, which does move that section's unit) is left in place.
findings.text: §55's Why asserts "That write changes the plan's whole-document digest, so review coverage reports the document unit uncovered", but `plan_review._without_section_bookkeeping` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:409-421, present since `3080646c90` on 2026-10-05) drops `section_declarations` and each section record's status/effort/attempts before the document digest is taken, and `CONTRACT_DOCUMENT_FIELDS` in the admission path is `("summary", "decisions", "gates")` (reckon/crew/routing.py:2782), so a done-declaration enters neither; measured on this plan's own snapshot, flipping `s46` implementable → done in both the declarations meta and the section element leaves `_section_digests` byte-identical for every unit ("doc same after declaration flip: True", "changed units: []"), and the same computation across two real declaration commits to `docs/plans/a-read-costs-what-changed.html` reports "changed units: []" and "doc moved: False" for `df7fae0058` and `7f11978888` — the reviews those commits supposedly triggered must have another trigger

findings.reason: the pair cannot both be green on one codebase: a node either reports a review owed where the shipped comparison owes none, or weakens the case, and the first case in isolation proves a guard that was already there.
findings.text: §55's first case ("records one section done with a close comment, and reads the plan still covered with no review composed") is already satisfied at the base revision with no code landed, because a declaration write moves no unit digest and a close comment is dropped by `_without_comments_and_followups` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:356-375), while its third case ("moves a section from done to implementable and reads a review owed") asserts the opposite and cannot pass at base because that write moves nothing either — the same probe returns no changed unit for a declaration flip in either direction

findings.reason: the citations illustrate a volume the mechanism finding already overturns, so restating the root cause replaces them.
findings.text: the run ids §55 cites as its evidence (`r-20261114T082056081169` and the four overnight reviews `r-20261113T194924849456`, `r-20261114T021654185885`, `r-20261114T041841066502`, `r-20261114T063500052018`) name no run this workstation can open: `reckon crew directory --run` reports "no live run" for `r-20261114T082056081169` and `r-20261113T194924849456`, and the a-read-costs-what-changed report tree holds `r-20261114T082047848049` and `r-20261113T161724909646` at those hours instead

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §55's third case asserts a review is owed for a declaration moving done → implementable, which no digest in the shipped code can make true, and its first case passes at the base revision with no work landed.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §55's gate log goes to the section's evidence fragment on a durable path, and the gate runs on `all_debug`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §55 introduces no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag, and its prose describes the record rather than the tracker entry.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §55's stated root cause is contradicted by the code at the reviewed revision: a declaration moving to done changes no review unit, so it cannot be what un-covered the document unit.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §55 names one deliverable: a declaration-only write owes no review.
